1. packages/react/src/components/DangerButton/DangerButton.js::DangerButton – this is the top‐level component for our danger style button. It currently just forwards kind="danger" to <Button> and never emits an aria-describedBy or visually hidden label. We need to extend this component to include a hidden <span> (e.g. “Danger!”) and set aria-describedBy on the wrapping <Button> so screen readers know the button is dangerous.

2. packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.js::Button – this core component is responsible for rendering assistive text for icon-only buttons but has no built-in support for danger semantics. We may choose instead to embed the danger assistive text here whenever kind === 'danger', or at a minimum ensure it correctly accepts and renders the aria-describedBy prop passed down by DangerButton. Fixes in Button.js will guarantee that the hidden span is rendered in the right place alongside children and icons, and that aria-describedBy attributes aren’t stripped out.

2.explanation: The only file that needs updating is DangerButton.js. The DangerButton component currently just forwards props into the core Button and does not inject any hidden text or ARIA relationships. To fix the issue, modify the DangerButton function to render the visually hidden Danger! as a child of the Button and add aria-describedby="danger-info" on the Button element it returns. This change will ensure that screen readers announce the danger state along with the button’s label.
